agent_self_modification_bypass.defect_claim: An agent can rewrite its own definition or the definitions that govern it, outside review.
premises: The cited agent definition grants the Edit or Write tool.
Nothing in the agent's dispatch (allowed scope, forbidden scope or a write gate) stops it from writing under .claude/agents/.

broad_shell_permission.defect_claim: A workflow grants write permissions its jobs do not need.
premises: The cited line grants write-all or contents: write to the workflow or a job.
No step in the jobs that receive the permission writes to the repository (push, release, tag, or a commit through the API).

direct_anthropic_api_usage.defect_claim: Code reaches the Anthropic API directly instead of through the approved wrapper.
premises: The cited file imports or calls @anthropic-ai/sdk.
The file runs in ARIA, CI or a product service, not in a test double, a type-only import or documentation.

lease_token_in_logs.defect_claim: A lease token is written where a reader of logs or stdout can replay it.
premises: The cited line writes a value derived from a lease token to a log, print or stdout sink.
The written value is the token or enough of it to replay, not a hash, a prefix-free reference or a redaction.

prompt_injection_surface.defect_claim: An agent that reads content an outside party can author runs without a tool allowlist or with unrestricted paths.
premises: The cited agent definition declares no tools allowlist, or allows every path (allowed_paths: **).
The agent is dispatched on content an outside party can author (pull request or issue text, fork code, review comments).

secret_leak_in_yaml_or_md.defect_claim: A usable credential is committed in a workflow, agent definition or ARIA source file.
premises: The cited line holds a credential value itself (key, token or password), not a placeholder, a variable reference or a secret-store lookup.
The value is not a documented dummy, test fixture or redacted example.

workflow_run_or_pr_target_untrusted_chec.defect_claim: A privileged workflow checks out code from an untrusted pull request and runs it with the base repository's secrets or write token.
premises: The workflow is triggered by pull_request_target or workflow_run.
A step checks out the pull request's head ref or head sha.
A later step builds, tests or executes the checked-out code while secrets or a write-scoped token are available to it.

base_event_field_missing.defect_claim: BaseEvent lacks a field every event must carry.
premises: The BaseEvent interface in libs/event-contracts does not declare the named field.
The field is not supplied by an interface BaseEvent extends.

create_base_event_missing.defect_claim: libs/event-contracts exposes no createBaseEvent factory, so event ids, timestamps, tenant ids and versions are minted inconsistently.
premises: libs/event-contracts does not export a createBaseEvent function.
Producers construct BaseEvent fields by hand instead of through another exported factory.

event_id_brand_missing.defect_claim: EventId is a plain string, so inline event construction compiles.
premises: BaseEvent's eventId is typed as an unbranded string in libs/event-contracts.
No other type-level construct in libs/event-contracts stops an event literal from assigning a plain string eventId.

schema_catalog_empty.defect_claim: A runtime event-schema catalog is empty, so runtime validation covers no event types.
premises: The cited catalog contains no schema entries.
The runtime validator dispatches events through this catalog, not through another populated one.

schema_catalog_not_wired_to_validator.defect_claim: An event-schema catalog is never consulted by the runtime validator, so its schemas validate nothing.
premises: The runtime validator dispatcher does not reference the cited catalog, directly or through an import.
The catalog holds schemas for events that cross a trust boundary at runtime.

controller_missing_guard_boundary.defect_claim: A route is reachable without the authentication or authorization its data requires.
premises: The cited route has no guard, role or permission decorator on the method or its class, and is not marked public.
No guard registered for the whole service (APP_GUARD, middleware or the gateway) protects the route.

dangerous_html_without_sanitizer.defect_claim: Markup that can carry attacker-controlled content is rendered unsanitized.
premises: The cited sink passes markup to dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitizing it first.
The markup can contain content a user or an external system supplies.

mutation_missing_role_boundary.defect_claim: A GraphQL mutation runs for any authenticated caller, without a role, permission or guard check.
premises: The cited mutation has no role, permission or guard decorator on the method or its class.
No guard registered for the whole service (APP_GUARD or the gateway) enforces a role or permission for it.

public_write_endpoint_without_allowlist.defect_claim: An unauthenticated caller can reach a write endpoint that no allowlist or tenant-skip rationale accounts for.
premises: The cited endpoint is marked public and performs a write (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE or a GraphQL mutation).
No allowlist entry, tenant-skip rationale or gateway rule restricts who can reach it.

raw_security_sensitive_import.defect_claim: A security-sensitive SDK is used directly instead of through the approved wrapper.
premises: The cited file imports the named SDK directly.
The file is runtime code outside the approved wrapper, not a test, a type-only import or the wrapper itself.

tenant_guard_missing.defect_claim: A service imports TenantGuard but never applies it, so requests run without tenant context enforcement.
premises: The cited module imports TenantGuard and registers no APP_GUARD for it.
No other mechanism (a controller-level guard on every route, middleware or the gateway) enforces tenant context for the service.

tenant_raw_query_missing_tenant_predicat.defect_claim: A raw SQL query can read or change another tenant's rows.
premises: The cited query touches a table shared across tenants, not a per-tenant table that search_path routes into the tenant's own schema.
Neither the query's predicate, row-level security nor the calling context restricts it to the current tenant.

tenant_repository_unscoped_read.defect_claim: A repository call can read or change another tenant's rows.
premises: The cited call reads or writes a table shared across tenants (a cross-tenant table, or one keyed by tenantId), not a per-tenant table that search_path routes into the tenant's own schema.
Neither the call's predicate, the repository helper, row-level security nor the caller restricts it to the current tenant.

high_risk_source_without_adjacent_test.defect_claim: A write boundary with behaviour of its own has no test that exercises it.
premises: The cited source performs writes and has behaviour beyond returning constants (it takes dependencies or computes results).
No unit, integration or e2e test imports it, sits beside it, or calls its route or GraphQL field.

migration_without_test.defect_claim: A migration that destroys or reshapes data has no test that runs it.
premises: The cited migration drops, deletes, truncates, alters a type of, or forces row-level security on live data.
No test or migration-check job runs this migration against a database and asserts its effect.

security_source_without_security_test.defect_claim: A guard implementation or a public write has no test that exercises its security behaviour.
premises: The cited source implements a guard (or authentication strategy) or exposes a write to unauthenticated callers.
No unit, integration or e2e test imports it, sits beside it, or calls its route or GraphQL field.

db_snapshot_column_missing.defect_claim: An entity column does not exist in the deployed table, so queries on it fail.
premises: The cited entity column is mapped (not a virtual, relation-only or excluded property).
The schema snapshot the finding names was taken from the deployed database and lacks the column.

db_snapshot_nullability_mismatch.defect_claim: An entity requires a value the database column allows to be null.
premises: The cited entity column is declared NOT NULL.
The deployed column, per the named snapshot, is nullable.

db_snapshot_table_missing.defect_claim: An entity's table does not exist in the database schema it is deployed against.
premises: The cited entity maps a table the service reads or writes at runtime.
The schema snapshot the finding names was taken from the database the service runs against and does not contain the table.

db_snapshot_uuid_type_mismatch.defect_claim: An entity declares a uuid column the database stores as another type.
premises: The cited entity column is declared uuid.
The deployed column's type, per the named snapshot, is not uuid.

migration_registry_missing_entry.defect_claim: A migration class exists but is not registered, so it never runs.
premises: The cited migration class is meant to run (it is not archived or superseded).
The service's migration registry does not include the class, directly or through a glob.

migration_registry_missing_file.defect_claim: A registered migration has no implementation, so the migration run fails or skips it.
premises: The service's migration registry names the cited class.
No migration file in the service declares the class.

module_schema_table_missing.defect_claim: An entity's table is absent from MODULE_SCHEMAS, so schema management does not create or check it.
premises: The cited entity maps a table the service owns.
MODULE_SCHEMAS for the service does not list the table, and no other registration covers it.

typeorm_entity_schema_required.defect_claim: An entity that must declare its schema does not, so its table can land in public.
premises: The cited @Entity() declares no literal schema option.
The table is not a per-tenant table that search_path routes into the tenant schema (it is cross-tenant, listed in MODULE_SCHEMAS infrastructureTables, or owned by a platform service).

bundle_budget_not_enforced.defect_claim: The module ships without a size budget that fails CI when its bundle grows past it.
premises: The module has a production Vite build (a vite config beside its package.json).
No bundle-budget.json beside the module and no CI workflow or build step fails when the module's bundle exceeds a declared size.

heavy_dependency_statically_imported.defect_claim: A heavyweight library is welded into the module's initial chunk by a static import.
premises: The cited line statically imports the named library in module source that ships in the production bundle.
The importing file is reachable from the module's entry without a dynamic import() or React.lazy boundary in between.

doc_references_missing_path.defect_claim: A document describes a repository path that no longer exists, so a reader is pointed at a surface that is gone.
premises: The cited line names the path as an existing part of the repository, not as a file to create, a removed file or a historical record.
The path does not exist in the repository at the judged commit, and no file it was renamed to is named beside it.

hand_copied_dto_field_drift.defect_claim: A frontend DTO hand-copied from a backend DTO has drifted, so the ValidationPipe strips or rejects fields and input is lost.
premises: The frontend type is a copy of the cited backend DTO, sent to or read from the endpoint that DTO validates.
The two field sets differ in a field the request or response actually carries.

cli_verb_never_routed.defect_claim: A kernel CLI subcommand parses but no branch dispatches it, so invoking it does nothing.
premises: The cited subcommand is registered on the kernel CLI parser.
No dispatch branch or handler mapping runs code for the subcommand.

policy_key_never_read.defect_claim: A kernel policy file declares a tunable that no kernel module reads, so setting it changes nothing.
premises: The cited key is declared in aria-kernel/aria_kernel/data/*.json as an operator tunable.
No kernel module reads the key, directly or through a loader that iterates the policy block.

*.defect_claim: The cited code has the defect the named lint rule describes.
premises: The cited line has the behaviour the named rule's message describes, in code that runs (not a test fixture, generated file or dead branch).
The behaviour is a defect in this context: a correct program would not keep it, rather than a style preference the codebase allows.

banned_phrase.defect_claim: A tracked, non-exempt file uses a phrase CLAUDE.md bans as a gating excuse for an unfinished fix.
premises: The cited line is prose or a code comment written by this repository, not a domain value, an identifier, a quoted rule list or third-party text.
The phrase on the cited line excuses leaving work unfinished, with no owner, deadline and tracked finding beside it.

controller_injects_repository_directly.defect_claim: A controller injects a TypeORM repository, skipping the service and bus layers (CLAUDE.md layer rule 1).
premises: The cited file is a NestJS controller that serves requests in production.
The cited line injects a TypeORM repository into the controller.

controller_skips_command_query_bus.defect_claim: A controller calls a TypeORM repository method directly instead of going through the command or query bus (CLAUDE.md layer rule 1).
premises: The cited file is a NestJS controller that serves requests in production.
The cited line calls a TypeORM repository, data source or entity manager method directly, and the controller does not route that operation through CommandBus or QueryBus.

dual_alias_missing.defect_claim: A module-resolution surface maps one backend-common root alias and not the other.
premises: The cited file is a module-resolution surface (tsconfig paths or jest moduleNameMapper) that a build, test or lint run uses.
The surface maps one backend-common root alias and has no mapping for the other.

dual_alias_target_drift.defect_claim: A module-resolution surface maps the two backend-common root aliases to different targets.
premises: The cited file is a module-resolution surface that a build, test or lint run uses.
The two backend-common root aliases resolve to different files in it.

domain_event_published_outside_outbox.defect_claim: A unit of work in a service that registers the outbox makes a durable write and then publishes the event with eventBus.publish instead of OutboxPublisher.enqueue, so the event and the write can diverge.
premises: The finding's second evidence line is a durable write (a repository or entity-manager save, insert, update or delete) made in the same method, or in a same-class helper it calls, before the cited publish.
The cited publish announces that state change as a domain event other services act on, not telemetry or a log.
The service registers OutboxModule.forFeature, so OutboxPublisher.enqueue is available to this unit of work.
